card.name: Shalakho
card.tagline: The Caucasus' fiery competitive courtship dance
card.profile: Shalakho (Շալախո) is a dynamic, acrobatic dance known throughout the Caucasus, including Armenia, Georgia and Azerbaijan. Its most common form features two or more men competing to attract a woman's attention, using swords or sticks and performing fast jumps, kicks and spins, while the woman moves with softer, shorter steps (NaTakallam; Armenian dance). It is a lively solo/competitive dance performed at public gatherings.
card.insight: As a shared Caucasian dance claimed by Armenian, Georgian and Azerbaijani traditions, shalakho illustrates the deeply intertwined performance cultures of the region, even as each group maintains its own version and styling (NaTakallam).
card.image_significance: Competitive men's solo showpiece. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — Caucasus, Armenia/Georgia.
